issue: Blocking a user who had already blocked the caller deleted the other owner's block row. The caller could then unblock and erase both parties' protection.
implementation: Preserve reverse blocked rows and create a separate directed block using the existing UNIQUE(user_id, friend_id) schema. Pair lookup prioritizes blocked records and then the caller-owned direction, making own unblock deterministic while preserving reverse enforcement.
verification: Targeted block/unblock service tests and TestFriendshipIndependentDirectedBlocks passed in Linux Go with count=1. Actual SQLite test verifies both directions select their own records, deleting one leaves IsBlocked true and the other owner's block list intact.

atomicConcurrency: TestAtomicBlockConcurrentReplacement passed count=10 on SQLite and actual PostgreSQL 18. Two simultaneous production atomic writers replace one accepted friendship; exactly one reports removing the relationship, both directed block lists contain one entry and accepted friend lists are empty. Wrapped DB path used. No-port temporary PostgreSQL container stopped and auto-removed.
acceptanceRace: TestAtomicBlockWinsConcurrentPendingAcceptance passed count=10 on SQLite and actual PostgreSQL 18. Races pending-row UpdateStatus(accepted) against production CreateBlockAtomic; accepts success or stale-row not-found for acceptance, requires successful block, final directed blocked row and empty accepted friend lists for both owners. Temporary no-port container stopped and auto-removed. This proves database state, not ordering of later WS/DM side effects.
lateFriendEvents: friendStore refuses own-blocked peers from request/accept WS events and late successful request/accept HTTP results; friend/request list reads filter currently own-blocked peers. Relationship removal clears friends plus incoming/outgoing requests. Seventeen friend/block store tests passed, including late accept after local block and stale event resurrection. Does not claim reverse-block event ordering or server DM side-effect completion.
dmAcceptanceGuard: Manual AcceptRequest and friendship-triggered AcceptPendingChannels recheck bidirectional block status before status write. Block or lookup failure stops write, acceptance event and notification settlement. New four-case service regression covers both paths and lookup failure; complete go test ./services passed in 21.700s. This is a service guard, not transaction-wide check/write atomicity.
conditionalDMTransition: Production DM repository now updates pending to accepted only if no directed block exists in the same SQL statement. Manual/automatic service paths use PendingDMAccepter capability and emit no success side effects if no row changed. Actual SQLite regression covers both block directions, preserved pending state, acceptance after unblock, duplicate acceptance and missing channel; targeted repository/service tests passed. This is statement-snapshot enforcement, not serialization against uncommitted concurrent blocks.
conditionalDMVerification: Actual PostgreSQL 18 conditional transition regression passed count=3, both block directions and pending/duplicate/missing cases. Six-case TestDMAcceptConditionalWriteGatesSideEffects passed: manual/automatic success emits two accept events after writer completion; unchanged returns conflict; failure propagates; neither rejected outcome settles notifications or falls back to unconditional update. Temporary no-port PostgreSQL container stopped and auto-removed.
dmBlockSerialization: Supersedes statement-only limitation above: production atomic block locks existing pair DM row before friendship mutation; pending acceptance opens WithTx, locks same DM row, then evaluates pending/block predicate in a separate statement (fresh PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED snapshot). SQLite targeted atomic/acceptance regressions passed. Actual PostgreSQL controlled open-transaction test held block uncommitted, observed accept waiting, committed block, then verified accept false and channel still pending. PostgreSQL lock/conditional/concurrent-block tests passed count=3. Temporary no-port database container stopped and auto-removed.
canonicalFriendAccept: Friend accept WS events now invalidate earlier relationship reads and refresh canonical friend/request lists rather than inserting stale event payloads. Thirty friend/block/WS tests passed including reverse-block late event and list/removal race; TypeScript and targeted ESLint passed. Network failure preserves last confirmed state rather than claiming event data is current.
friendHTTPCompletion: All friend mutation completions check captured account/auth generation before local effects. Twenty-one friend/block tests passed including late HTTP acceptance after reverse removal and send success after account switch; TypeScript and targeted ESLint passed.
